title: Personal batching oddball triage
content:
Objective:
Quick personal trail of breadcrumbs while investigating sudden throughput regressions on Hosted API (region: us-west-2) after the last runtime deploy (PR 1834). Notes are messy — for my own handoff if I get pulled into pager.

Summary of observed problem:
- Baseline throughput for embeddings endpoints dropped ~25% for short requests (seq_len ~64) after deploy on 2026-02-27.
- Latency p50 stable, p95 increased slightly; token-per-second decreased.
- CPU/GPU utilization on dedicated backends looked normal, but request queueing increased.

Initial hypotheses (quick):
1) Continuous-batching (cbatch) policy misconfigured: window too long or batching threshold increased.
2) KV-prefetch or prefix cache logic changed causing more cache misses and extra compute.
3) Kernel selection fallback picking slower kernels for small sequences due to dynamic dispatch bug.
4) Autoscaler/worker churn causing more cold-starts and smaller batch sizes.

Commands & checks I ran (chronological):
- Grepped logs for new cBatch flags:
  $ rg "cbatch|continuous_batch|batch_window" -n /var/log/redwood/runtime-2026-*
  found: runtime-config: continuous_batch.window_ms=120, continuous_batch.min_batch=4 (expected 30ms / min_batch=2).

- Queried runtime config via admin API:
  $ curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin-usw2.redwood.internal/runtime/config | jq '.continuous_batch'
  => {"window_ms":120, "min_batch":4, "max_wait_percentile":95}
  (this is the diff from prod doc where we usually use window_ms=30, min_batch=2)

- Replayed traffic (local replay) with same request mix:
  - baseline (window 30ms / min_batch 2) QPS 500 => mean TPS 2300 tokens/s
  - changed to current (window 120ms / min_batch 4) QPS 500 => mean TPS 1650 tokens/s
  => ~28% drop which matches observed.

Error snippets and logs:
- Worker logs (serving-runtime):
  2026-02-28T03:14:21.112Z WARN batching: delaying batch send (window exceeded) window_ms=120 current_batch_size=3
  2026-02-28T03:14:21.113Z INFO kernel-select: fallback to kernel v2-slow for model openlm-7b at seq_len=64
  2026-02-28T03:14:21.200Z INFO cache: kv-prefetch miss key=ctx-uid-xxxx

- Admin traces (shortened):
  route: /v1/embeddings -> route-handler -> batching-layer -> executor
  batching-layer duration increased by 85ms on average (matches window bump)

Immediate conclusions from these checks:
- The continuous_batch.window_ms / min_batch parameters were changed in the last deploy. That alone plausibly explains batching inefficiency for short sequences.
- The kernel fallback line is suspicious — check why dispatcher chose v2-slow for seq_len=64 (we expect fast kernels optimized for small seqs). Might be due to a model-arch tag mismatch introduced in PR 1834.

Quick mitigations I tried (dev-env patching):
1) Toggled window back to 30ms and min_batch=2 via admin API for a canary pool:
  $ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"continuous_batch": {"window_ms": 30, "min_batch": 2}}' https://admin-usw2.redwood.internal/runtime/config/apply?pool=canary-a
  Observed canary: throughput recovered to within 5% of baseline, p95 reduced.
2) Forced kernel selection override for canary model to prefer v1-fast:
  $ admin runtime kernel-override --model openlm-7b --kernel v1-fast --pool canary-a
  Observed additional small boost.
3) Disabled kv-prefetch for canary (flip off prefetch flag): small improvement in cold-start churn but not major.

Things to investigate next (ordered):
- Why were batch params changed: check PR 1834 (linked). Was this intentional tuning? Look at PR description and deployment notes.
- Why kernel dispatcher chose slower kernel: inspect new kernel selection logic (serving-runtime/kernel_selector.go) changes in PR 1834. Suspect wrong heuristics based on sequence-length percentiles being mis-computed.
- Confirm whether autoscaler changed target utilization or cooldown that increases worker churn (look at infra/autoscaler deploys between 2026-02-25 and 2026-02-28).
- Re-run long A/B with production traffic mix to ensure no regressions for long sequences after reverting batch params.

Hypotheses to validate with metrics and experiments:
- H1: Batch window increase -> larger inter-request wait times for small seqs -> lower batch density for short inputs -> throughput drop. (Validated by replay and canary revert)
- H2: Kernel fallback aggregated with longer batching window -> combined penalty -> worse p95. (Partially validated by kernel override test)
- H3: Change intended to smooth high variance for long sequence workloads but not gated by route-specific policies (mistake: global change instead of per-route).

Notes for handoff / next steps for the team:
- Revert global batch params in next cut or make them route-specific. Follow-up with PR author @samir about intent.
- Add test in CI that replays a small-seq traffic mix and asserts >90% of kernels used are v1-fast for seq_len <=128.
- Add observability metric: continuous_batch.window_ms per pool as a time-series and alert if above 50ms for embeddings routes.
- Add a small unit test to kernel_selector that ensures for model-arch X and seq_len<128, preferred kernel list contains v1-fast before v2-slow.

Random scratch commands / notes I left below for myself:
- Dump config of pool that saw worst regression:
  $ admin runtime pool describe pool-prod-a --format yaml > pool-prod-a.yaml
- Compare config diffs between canary and prod:
  $ diff -u pool-prod-a.yaml pool-canary-a.yaml | rg "continuous_batch|kernel" -n
- Quick perf replay harness (local):
  go run tools/replay/main.go --trace samples/embeddings_short_mix.json --rate 300 --runtime-endpoint https://canary-usw2.redwood.internal

Open questions / unknowns:
- Who changed the default from 30ms->120ms? Deploy notes mention "batching improvements" but not values. Need to chase deployment changelog.
- Did autoscaler changes coincidentally influence effective batch sizes? Need correlation between worker churn and batch sizes over time.
- Are there any downstream customers affected (alerts triggered)? CC: customer success if SLA impacted.

If I get pulled into pager, leave this doc link in the slack thread and ping Samir and Lina. Will update with final decision (revert vs route-scoped tuning).

-- Ava
